lesson.menu_title: Getting the Words Right — Plans, Decisions and Commitments
lesson.menu_desc: Verbs followed by -ing or to, for the decisions and promises that come out of every meeting -- 34 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 13 -- Getting the Words Right
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Rosa M. Mitiko Shida | Lesson 13 -- Getting the Words Right

listenings.text: Hi Rosa, it is Andres from the Santiago office. I am calling about the regional meeting. We have decided to move it to September, and I wanted you to hear it from me before the email goes out. I know the team was looking forward to meeting in Lima, and I am sorry about that. The problem is the budget. We simply cannot afford to fly twelve people in before the new fares are approved. I would suggest keeping the Thursday call as planned, because there are two clients who refuse to wait until September for an answer. And one more thing. Please remember to send me the revised proposal before Friday. Last time we managed to agree on everything in the room and then forgot to write it down. I do not want to make that mistake twice. Call me if you need anything.

Most meetings end with a decision, and most decisions die in the week after. In my experience, the problem is rarely the decision itself. It is that everybody agrees to do something and nobody arranges a time to do it. So here are three habits. First, before you leave the room, name the person who has agreed to act, and the date. Do not leave it as we should consider changing the process. Second, if you cannot afford the time this week, say so. Refusing politely is more professional than accepting and doing nothing. And third, admit mistakes early. A colleague who says I forgot to send the figures on Monday is easy to work with. A colleague who keeps promising to send them is not. Decisions do not fail in the meeting. They fail when people stop following up.

items.situation: Your client in Santiago keeps canceling meetings. What do you suggest?
tips: I suggest moving the meeting to a fixed day every month

items.situation: Your team failed to hit the Q2 target. What do you admit to the director?
tips: I admit underestimating how long the Lima launch would take

items.situation: The Buenos Aires office has just opened. What do you plan to do differently?
tips: We plan to visit the ten biggest clients in the first month

items.situation: A client asks for a discount you cannot give. What do you say?
tips: I am afraid we cannot afford to lower the fare again

items.situation: Your manager asks if you sent the revised proposal. You did, last week.
tips: I remember sending it on Tuesday

items.situation: A colleague is spending hours on a slide deck that nobody will read. Give advice.
tips: I would avoid spending more time on it

extra_audio.text: Julio tells Rosa that the director decided to postpone the regional meeting until the third quarter. Rosa says she is not surprised, because Santiago kept asking for more time. Julio explains that the director suggested reviewing the whole proposal and refused to sign it as it was. He admits forgetting to send the Lima figures, although he remembers sending the draft. Rosa decides to arrange a call with Santiago for Thursday and asks Julio to give the new format a shot.
